newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Oct 24.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The underlying inflation measure is now in the Reserve Bank's target zone of two to three per cent for the first time since June 1995, following the release of Consumer Price Index figures yesterday which showed the CPI fell to 2.1 per cent after prices rose 0.3 per cent in the September quarter. Treasurer Peter Costello said the result indicates inflation is no longer a "speed limit" on Australia's economic growth. Page 1.

The Maritime Union of Australia announced yesterday it had negotiated a deal with Mobil, BP and Australian Petroleum to retain the crude oil tanker, the Canopus, in the Australian trade in a bid to stop the push by major oil companies to cut back on their use of Australian-crewed tankers in shipping crude oil. Page 2.

According to a Mastercard International survey, nearly a quarter of Singaporeans, Japanese and South Koreans said Australia was the best country in the region to live in and more than 20 per cent of Singaporeans, Indonesians and Japanese surveyed said Australia was the best country for personal investment in real estate. Page 3.

Addressing the Australian Society of Certified Practising Accountants' conference in Melbourne yesterday, Prime Minister and Cabinet Department secretary Max Moore-Wilton said the Federal Public Service Act was far too complex and required fundamental change. Moore-Wilton said the Act had resulted in a "process-driven culture suffocating under the weight of rules and regulations with an entitlement mentality". Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Speaking to the Committee for the Economic Development of Australia yesterday, Treasury head Ted Evans denied criticisms of the Government's Workplace Relations Bill, claiming that radical industrial relations reforms were an essential step in cutting unemployment. However, Evans conceded that the unemployment rate would remain close to eight per cent until at least the year 2000. Page 1.

Contrary to Federal Government assertions that Australia's rift with France has been repaired, senior United Nations and United States officials confirmed yesterday that France had played a key role in thwarting Australia's bid to win a seat on the UN Secrity Council by backing Portugal in retaliation for last year's bitter row over nuclear testing in the South Pacific. Page 1.

The Federal Opposition was last night calling for the resignation of Employment Minister Amanda Vanstone after officers from Vanstone's Department of Employment, Training and Youth Affairs told a Senate estimates committee that the department had provided the former Labor Government with a scenario under which a five per cent unemployment goal was achievable, despite comments by Vanstone in August and last month that Labor was told before the election the five per cent jobless target was "not achievable". Page 1.

As part of sweeping changes to Victorian Education, the Kennett Government will seek to merge 113 primary and secondary schools, cut 100 Education Department administrative jobs, impose 10 per cent budget cuts across central and regional offices and cut funding to early literacy, English and disadvantaged school programs. In the first general offer of voluntary redundancies by the Victorian Government since 1992-93, more than 600 teaching positions are expected to be targeted. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Although annual growth in the Consumer Price Index dropped a full one percentage point to 2.1 per cent in the September quarter, strengthening the case for a cut in interest rates when the Reserve Bank board meets on November 5, Federal Treasurer Peter Cotello has urged caution, suggesting that wage settlements will have to be "carefully monitored". Page 1.

Safety in the schoolyard has come under the spotlight again, after a 14-year-old schoolboy was charged with attempted murder last night following an incident at Marrickville High School yesterday where teacher Russell Edwards was chased and stabbed twice in the back with a 25cm knife. Page 1.

The Police Royal Commission heard yesterday that former detective inspector John Wilson withheld information on three unsolved Sydney gangland murders given to him by two Long Bay jail inmates. The police officer also rejected an offer from one of the prisoners to wear a listening device to get more information from his cell mate. Page 1.

Just four days before the Australian stockmarket float of Stadium Australia, the company formed to build and operate the A$465 million Sydney Olympic stadium, ANZ Bank wrote to Stadium Australia's financial manager, Tower Hill Investment Managers, expressing its anger at Tower Hill receiving a corporate box for free use by managers and their friends. ANZ said the deal was "flawed and against the spirit of the transaction". Page 1.
THE AGE

The Victorian Opposition was calling for the immediate resignation of Victorian solicitor-general Douglas Graham QC last night after it was discovered Graham - who last year advised the State Government against prosecuting BHP for contempt - has been linked to four family companies that are significant shareholders in the steel and minerals giant. Page A1.

The Victorian solicitor-general, who was a leading barrister before taking up the post four years ago, claims he has not breached clause 37 of the Code of Conduct for the State's public sector, which requires public servants to discuss with their "approprate manager" any potential areas of conflict of interest, over directorships in companies that held shares in BHP. Page A1.

In the biggest education revamp since the Victorian Government closed 300 schools and made 8,000 teachers redundant, the State Government has marked 113 schools for voluntary closure - 86 primary schools and 18 secondary schools - and confirmed a new round of redundancies for hundreds of teachers. Page A1.

In his opening defence to the County Court yesterday against conspiracy and bribery charges, Con Heliotis QC, for property developer Bruno Grollo, said Grollo was convinced someone in the Australian Federal Police or the office of the director of public prosecutions was after him and he hired a private investigator to help prove it. Page A3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
